_comment: Example token set for a Brand Engine. This is the shared DNA layer: every primitive in the system reads from these values instead of defining its own color, depth, or motion. Swap values per client -- the structure is what's reusable.

color.rule: signal.primary is the only saturated hue in the system. It never appears at more than 15% surface coverage per viewport -- used for emphasis, not fill.

depth.rule: All primitives share one shadow color and blur falloff curve, regardless of shape, so depth reads as one material rather than per-element effects.

grain.rule: A constant low-opacity noise overlay sits above every primitive to unify surface texture across otherwise different geometries.

motion.rule: Every primitive responds to the same input (pointer position) with the same easing curve and a depth-proportional parallax offset, so a multi-primitive composition moves as one object, not several.

geometry.rule: All directional primitives (arrows, facets, motion lines) resolve to the same 45-degree axis. This is what lets shapes combine without visually fighting each other.

combination_rules: Primitives may appear alone or together; never more than 2 in a single composition.
When combined, one primitive must be visually dominant (60/40 minimum split) -- no primitive pairing may compete at equal weight.
signal.primary may only be applied to one primitive at a time in a shared composition.
Grain and depth tokens are mandatory on every primitive instance; geometry.axis is mandatory on every directional element.
